sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong influence of French law and EU-derived statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States DTA (1996, as amended by 2009 protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 13 January 2010 on the register of beneficial owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 27 July 2018 and subsequent implementing regulations; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 relating to the Register of Beneficial Owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (if pre-incorporated draft)
Certificate of Good Standing / Excerpt from foreign registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national ID of each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the person's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (if not Hague Apostille signatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address of shareholder and/or UBO
Bank reference letter for each founder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (if not Hague Apostille signatory)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorised signatories against Luxembourg FIU (CRF), CSSF sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, family member, or close associate as defined by FATF Recommendation 12. Continuous monitoring under Luxembourg AML/CFT law and CSSF Circular 20/744.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – LBR (www.lbr.lu), operated by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in French, German, or Luxembourgish; if a name contains characters not native to these languages, a transliteration into Latin script is required. The name must be clearly distinguishable from all existing registered names and protected trade names in the RCSL. Use of foreign scripts without Latin transliteration is not accepted. The legal form designation 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' must appear in the name in an acceptable form, either fully written out or as the abbreviation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a formal appeal with the RCSL within 15 days of receipt of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written submission demonstrating that the proposed name meets distinctiveness and public order requirements. If the RCSL maintains rejection, the applicant may apply to the Tribunal de l'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Administrative Chamber) for judicial review within one month of the final administrative decision. Legal representation by a Luxembourg-qualified lawyer is mandatory for judicial appeals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are generally not permitted as a registered office for an SCSp that intends to carry on active commercial operations, including a B2B marketplace; the registered office must be a real physical address in Luxembourg where the central administration and statutory records are kept, accessible to the RCSL and tax authorities. The RCSL requires the registered office to be a physical location in Luxembourg; purely virtual addresses (e.g., mail-forwarding-only) are insufficient for substance requirements, especially for an SCSp seeking pass-through tax treatment and eligibility under EU directives.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (approx. 20–35% annual probability for newly registered entities in the e-commerce sector under CSSF and tax administration random inspection programs; unannounced on-site inspections may occur particularly if inconsistencies are found in VAT registration, substance documentation, or UBO data.)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL name reservation and availability check fee (application per name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Grand-Ducal Regulation on RCSL fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation of articles of association and partnership deed (drafting and execution before a Luxembourg notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for notarial services; range USD 1,200–2,000 for a standard SCSp deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial RCSL registration filing (inscription au registre de commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under RCSL fee schedule, excluding publication fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in the Official Gazette (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés – RES)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice / RCSL publication service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff per page; estimated USD 120–200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) initial UBO filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No fee for initial filing (free of charge) by law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address setup (lease or commercial office space, first quarter pro-rated)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private landlord or licensed corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rent in Luxembourg City / Kirchberg area; estimated USD 1,200–1,800 per quarter for a serviced office with meeting room access

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO and PEP screening software setup and initial screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Regtech service provider (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv, or Luxembourg-approved local provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial benchmark for SME onboarding, initial configuration plus screening of up to 10 individuals

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalisation and apostille processing (for shareholder documents, translations, and certifications)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassies/consulates, apostille authorities, and certified translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing government tariffs and professional translation rates; estimated USD 400–800 depending on country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local legal counsel fee for pre-incorporation due diligence and drafting of partnership deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a fixed-scope SCSp incorporation, including UBO clearance and name clearance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal, statutory registers, filing binder, and internal compliance kit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate; valued added at actual cost

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (particularly Articles 1, 14, 15-1 and Title IV concerning special limited partnerships); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 May 2010 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), R.C.S. Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Written partnership deed (contrat de société) and declaration of registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers; filing is made electronically via the LBR eDesk portal, followed by publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; contributions are freely determined by the partnership agreement. No escrow account or capital blocking requirement applies to an SCSp.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-forma first resolution of the founding general partner of the SCSp: RESOLVED that the SCSp is established under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; that the partnership deed is approved and adopted; that the capital contributions of the limited partners are accepted with no statutory minimum; that the registered office is fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; that [name] is appointed general partner and [name] is appointed manager for registration and administration; that all filings before the Luxembourg Business Registers and publication in RESA are authorized; that bank account opening is authorized; and that all costs incurred in the formation are ratified and payable by the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online consultation interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a preliminary name search through the LBR website or in person at the RCS counter to ensure the proposed SCSp name is distinguishable from existing corporate and partnership names. No formal reservation is mandatory, but an LBR clearance printout is recommended before deed drafting.
required_dossiers: Identity document or passport copy of the founding partner
Letter of intent (if the name is to be reserved)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or deemed confusingly similar, submit amended name variants and re-apply immediately; no filing fee is lost for a pure name check.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or private parties under Luxembourg civil law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership deed (acte de société) in French, German, or Luxembourgish. For an SCSp, the deed may be executed as a private writing signed by all partners or, if preferred for real estate transfers or compliance, as a notarial deed. The deed must identify the general partner, the limited partners, the amount and nature of contributions, the registered office address, and the management powers.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of all general and limited partners
Proof of address of each partner

Draft partnership deed containing the exact corporate name, registered office, object (ISIC 4791 – operation of an electronic B2B wholesale marketplace), contribution schedule, and partner liability clauses
Certificate of good standing (if a partner is a legal entity)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the enforceability of a private deed, execute a rectification deed or a notarial acknowledgment; the deed may be re-executed with corrected provisions without substantive penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – eDesk electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the LBR eDesk, submit the registration form (société en commandite spéciale) and upload the executed partnership deed, the declaration of conformity (déclaration concernant la constatation de la conformité), and the identity documents. Pay the statutory filing fee online. The RCS will assign the registration number; third parties have effect against the filing once published.
required_dossiers: Board/general partner resolution authorizing the filing
Valid passport/ID of the applicant and each partner
Proof of registered office address (lease or free-use consent)
Payment confirmation of the €19.50–25 electronic filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for clarification, respond within one month with corrected documents or explanatory submissions; a negative decision can be cured by resubmitting a technically compliant deed, without losing priority except in exceptional cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA publication unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR automatically transmits the registration data to RESA for mandatory legal publication. This publication perfects the third-party effectiveness of the SCSp's constitution. The entity obtains its RCS number and LEI (if required for financial services).
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate issued after step 3
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or contains typographical errors, file a written rectification request with the LBR; corrections to the partnership deed require a supplementary amending deed to be re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration fiscal, VAT, social security, and bank account formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); commercial banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Luxembourg VAT number by registering with the AEDT for cross-border B2B platform activity; register with the CCSS for any employees and social security obligations; open a corporate bank account. If the SCSp will hold immovable property, also register for property tax. No operating license is required for a pure electronic B2B marketplace under current Luxembourg law.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity for all partners and authorized signatories
Description of planned cross-border electronic platform operations
Bank account opening forms and due diligence information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is queried, provide a detailed business plan identifying the precise B2B wholesale platform model; any tax-specific issue should be resolved with AEDT through an electronic correspondence mechanism within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A – no industrial license required for an electronic B2B wholesale marketplace operator under Luxembourg law; such operators are not considered industrial establishments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: N/A – the business scope is ISIC 4791 / NAICS 425120 (electronic wholesale platform); no operating or manufacturing permit applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Agency – Administration de l'environnement, Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required: the activity is an information-technology service activity without physical production, discharge, or emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the digital platform itself. If later the company operates physical servers, warehouses, or offices, compliance with Luxembourg waste management, wastewater discharge, and VOC thresholds under the Umweltverwaltung will be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil defense or occupational clearance applies for a purely digital platform. If the SCSp opens commercial offices or warehousing, the employer must submit a workplace notice to the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and obtain a fire safety clearance from the Compagnie Grand-Ducale des Sapeurs-Pompiers (CGDIS) prior to occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes (portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (portal: https://aedt.public.lu); central business e-governance portal: https://guichet.lu; Luxembourg Business Registers portal: https://www.lbr.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SCSp formed in Luxembourg, the general partner must complete RCS registration through the Luxembourg Business Registers; this generates the national business registration number. For direct taxation, the SCSp itself is tax-transparent, so partners are identified through their own Luxembourg or foreign tax IDs; a Luxembourg tax number (NIF) may be obtained from the ACD via ordinary taxpayer registration if any partner is subject to Luxembourg tax. For VAT, if the SCSp is considered a taxable person carrying out an economic activity in its own name, a VAT registration application must be filed electronically with the AEDT through the MyGuichet / eTVA portal. Non-established foreign entities engaged in taxable Luxembourg B2B marketplace sales must register directly with the AEDT and appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative where required; the application must provide RCS extracts, identity of the general partner, proof of activity, and expected turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory default; no US-style check-the-box election exists. No election may be made to treat the SCSp as a taxable corporation for Luxembourg direct-tax purposes. Anti-hybrid rules under EU/ATAD II may re-characterise the entity or its partners in cross-border situations. For VAT, the SCSp may optionally join a Luxembourg VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') where legally established entities forming together a single taxable person so elect under the approval requirements of the AEDT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for established Luxembourg taxable persons; non-resident suppliers have no threshold and must register from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg unless an alternative rule (e.g., reverse charge, OSS/IOSS) applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping for B2B e-invoicing. E-invoices are legally accepted provided they preserve authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility. B2G e-invoicing is handled through the PEPPOL network where mandated. There is no general API-based real-time VAT reporting obligation for B2B marketplace operators at present.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available for supplies of goods physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods leave the EU and the exporter retains satisfactory proof. Zero rating also applies to intra-Community supplies to a registered EU customer. For services, zero rating or exclusion from Luxembourg VAT applies where the place of supply is outside the EU under Articles 44-48 of the Luxembourg VAT law (e.g., B2B services to a non-EU taxable person), or where services are directly connected with exported goods and satisfy documentary conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / ECS export declaration)
Bill of Lading (or equivalent transport document such as CMR consignment note or Air Waybill)
Inward Remittance Certificate (where applicable, evidencing foreign currency receipt and value transfer)
Proof of physical departure of goods from EU territory (e.g., customs stamp or electronic exit record)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may scrutinise export zero-rating claims retroactively and require the complete evidentiary bundle above within the statutory retention period. Missing, false, or fraudulent export documentation exposes the taxpayer to immediate VAT reassessment at 17%, acceleration of due VAT, statutory late-interest, and administrative fines ranging from 10% to 50% of the evaded VAT, plus criminal penalties in cases of intentional fraud. Refunds of input VAT linked to improperly zero-rated exports are clawed back with interest; repeat violations may also lead to loss of VAT group privileges and public procurement disqualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as the national central bank of the euro area and supervisory counterparty for balance-of-payments statistics; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent national authority for banking licensing, AML/CFT supervision and payment-institution oversight; the European Central Bank (ECB) holds ultimate monetary and exchange-rate policy authority for the euro.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible, and Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control restrictions on current-account transactions, capital-account movements, profit remittances, partnership distributions, liquidation proceeds or service fees. Free movement of capital with third countries is guaranteed under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, subject only to EU sanctions and prudential safeguards. For the Luxembourg SCSp, which is fiscally transparent, foreign partners are taxed directly at their residence level; no Luxembourg withholding tax applies to distributions of profits or to liquidation proceeds from the SCSp except in limited cases where the partnership is treated as opaque. Consequently, there is no regulatory currency-conversion bottleneck for treasury activity; the only residual obligations are statutory bank reporting to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes and customer due diligence under CSSF regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg statutory law does not impose any deadline for the repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio into euro, and no obligation to surrender foreign currency earned from cross-border B2B marketplace sales. The SCSp may lawfully hold USD, CNY, EUR or any other settlement currency in its multi-currency operational accounts, and the decision to convert proceeds is a treasury optimization decision rather than a regulatory requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Treasury Account with SWIFT and trade finance capabilities
Operational Account with SEPA, TARGET2 and SWIFT access, supplemented by escrow sub-accounts
Operational Account with USD clearing desk, documentary letter of credit issuance and cross-border payment rails
Operational Treasury Account with FX dealing and wealth-linked cash management services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in EUR with standard cash management and SEPA connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High. A Luxembourg-licensed or EEA-passported Electronic Money Institution may lawfully provide collection, payout and multi-currency treasury services to the SCSp under the PSD2 legal framework, provided client funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts at an EU authorized credit institution. Offshore digital EMIs not authorized in the EEA cannot act as the primary payment account provider for a Luxembourg resident merchant without breaching Luxembourg reserved-payment-activity rules. The recommended architecture is therefore a CSSF-supervised commercial bank as the primary settlement bank, with the fintech EMI or Alibaba Pay treasury gateway used as a supplementary collection and supplier-disbursement layer, subject to contractual safeguarding and audit rights.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is required in the standard onboarding process. The authorized manager of the general partner, or the Luxembourg-appointed representative, and each beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the SCSp must attend an in-person identity verification interview at the bank's premises or before a Luxembourg notary. Remote video-identification with an EU-recognized eID is technically permitted under the AML/CFT legal framework, but most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks retain the commercial right to demand an in-person meeting for cross-border trading entities with foreign principals. The SCSp should therefore budget for a physical signing ceremony in Luxembourg City and the appointment of a local authorized signatory to reduce operational friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity arising from the split general-partner and limited-partner structure of the SCSp, including corporate UBO chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier comprising the current Luxembourg RCS extract, the official beneficial-owner register certificate or filing confirmation, an ownership chart traced to natural persons, the limited partnership agreement of the SCSp, the constitutional documents of the corporate general partner, and the general partner's resolution authorizing the account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds scrutiny on an inbound equity contribution exceeding EUR 500,000 from a non-EU investor or from an Alibaba Pay settlement payout
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier comprising the investor's bank statements and source-of-wealth declaration, audited financial statements or tax returns of the contributing partner, the capital call letter issued by the general partner, the B2B marketplace service agreement, platform settlement statements from Alibaba Pay, the underlying trade order ledger, and the invoice trail for the commercial flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax pass-through and economic substance validation for a fiscally transparent SCSp engaged in cross-border e-commerce
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier comprising the Luxembourg advance tax ruling confirming fiscal transparency, the substance file with the Luxembourg lease agreement, payroll records, board minutes, platform hosting and data-processing contracts, warehouse or logistics agreements, and a written description of the management and control exercised at the Luxembourg principal place of business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or sanctions screening flags raised against treasury officers, limited partners or counterparty banks in the cross-border payment chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier comprising completed political-exposure questionnaires, World-Check or equivalent screening reports, written declarations that no person is subject to EU financial sanctions, the compliance policy of the platform operator, and the legal opinion confirming that the payment routing does not involve a sanctioned jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank surveillance red flag caused by frequent high-value payouts to suppliers in jurisdictions regarded as high-risk for trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier comprising customs declarations, air or sea waybills, packing lists, import and export entries, supplier contracts, product photographs with pricing confirmation, AEO certificate if available, and the reconciliation report matching each payout to an order number and invoice in the B2B marketplace system.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investor capital contributions shall be remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the SCSp capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance instruction must reference the SCSp RCS registration number, the capital-call letter reference, and the payment narrative 'contribution to partnership capital of a Luxembourg special limited partnership'. The receiving bank will classify the credit for BCL balance-of-payments statistics under the BPM6 direct-investment equity category (FA.5); no central-bank authorization is required. Marketplace-treasury inflows from the Alibaba Pay settlement engine, representing B2B platform sales or commission revenue, shall be remitted to the SCSp operational account with the payment narrative identifying the platform settlement statement and the service-income nature of the transaction; the bank will record these as service receipts under the current account of the balance of payments with the underlying invoice and order-level settlement reconciliation attached to the credit file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier disbursements within the EU shall be settled through SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 pain.001 messages across TARGET2 or STEP2 clearing, with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for time-critical payments. For third-country suppliers, particularly merchandise suppliers in China, the United States or Hong Kong, the primary clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer directly to the supplier's account, while larger-value transactions may be structured through a documentary commercial letter of credit issued under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700 and settled through the issuing bank's trade finance desk. The B2B marketplace payout obligation to Alibaba Pay or its acquiring treasury should be executed via the bank's SWIFT gateway, with each payout carrying the order identifier, invoice number and platform reconciliation code. All outbound disbursements must be underpinned by the underlying commercial invoice, transport document and customs entry to satisfy bank-level trade verification and AML controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forward contracts traded OTC under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Luxembourg-authorized EU bank
EUR/CNH nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge CNY-denominated supplier payables where onshore deliverability is constrained
EUR/USD cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for term financing or working-capital exposure alignment
Collared forward and participating forward structures executed within the SCSp treasury policy and MiFID II professional-client classification

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17.00% national corporate income tax; plus 7.00% unemployment-fund solidarity surcharge on CIT; plus municipal business tax (Luxembourg City standard rate 6.75%); aggregate headline Luxembourg City rate equals 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays. Applicable reliefs include the Luxembourg IP box (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, EU directives and DTA reliefs. The SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to CIT; profits and losses flow through to partners and are taxed at partner level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; subject to anti-abuse rules on change of ownership or activity for a corporate-taxed entity; for a transparent SCSp, loss character and utilization are determined at partner level)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 600 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and SCSp partner-allocation annex, filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / MyDossier tax portal maintained by the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax year is normally the calendar year; the annual return is due by 31 May of the following year. The tax administration may grant extensions; electronically filed returns are generally expected before the extended administrative deadline of 31 December where extension is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal form, RCS registration number, Luxembourg business address, and indication of transparent tax classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the correct Luxembourg registration data of the SCSp; do not refer to a foreign address. Attach the partner registry schedule identifying every non-resident partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Place of effective management and local substance indicators: office, employees, management decisions, bank account, board minutes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If effective management is outside Luxembourg, disclose the fact and assess treaty permanent establishment exposure. An address-only SCSp is a fatal red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial income or loss from the B2B cross-border marketplace operation (ISIC 4791).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the Luxembourg-source profit allocable to non-resident partners. The SCSp itself is not assessed; the amount must be reconciled with the partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable and exempt income items, including qualifying participation exemption income or IP box deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach legal basis for each exemption and identify the non-resident partner to whom the exempt income is allocated. Exemptions must be substantiated by title, economic substance, and ownership period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilized during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, utilization occurs in the hands of each partner under its residence country rules; Luxembourg loss carryforward rules apply only to Luxembourg-resident partners and to the partnership if it becomes corporate-taxed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner allocation matrix: partner names, tax residence, profit-sharing percentage, allocated income, and taxes withheld or paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory annex for non-resident partners. Each non-resident partner must provide a tax residence certificate to evidence treaty entitlement and beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default assessment (taxation d'office), late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, and administrative fines generally up to EUR 5,000 per return. Intentional concealment may escalate to criminal tax fraud penalties including higher fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15.00% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a resident non-transparent company. For a transparent SCSp, distributions to partners are generally characterized as profit withdrawals or capital distributions and are not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax. If the SCSp is corporate-taxed or a distribution is recharacterized as a deemed dividend under anti-abuse rules, the statutory 15.00% rate applies subject to DTA relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief is claimed at partner level, not at SCSp level. The non-resident partner must (i) obtain a tax residence certificate from its country of residence, (ii) provide the certificate and a beneficial ownership statement to the Luxembourg payer or the ACD before distribution for reduced withholding at source, (iii) rely on the applicable DTA and PPT/LoB safeguards, and (iv) if withholding was levied, file a timely refund claim with the Luxembourg tax administration. MAP and the EU Arbitration Convention are available where treaty relief is wrongfully denied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law does not impose withholding tax on interest or royalty payments to non-residents. Under many Luxembourg tax treaties and under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, cross-border interest and royalties paid to associated EU companies may benefit from a 0% or reduced treaty rate, subject to beneficial ownership and economic substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Reporting and Master File threshold: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue. Luxembourg does not publish a numeric Local File threshold, but any material cross-border controlled transaction should be documented. In practice, the tax administration requests Local File documentation within 30 days for transactions exceeding generally accepted materiality levels, including intercompany management fees, platform service fees, and goods procurement flows.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no separate Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the substance doctrine is embedded in domestic abuse-of-law rules, OECD BEPS PPT principles, EU ATAD, and administrative practice. An SCSp must maintain a Luxembourg registered office, local directors or managers, real decision-making, employees, adequate capital, a bank account, commercial contracts, and transfer pricing documentation. A shell SCSp used only as a tax-transparent invoice conduit for a foreign B2B platform will be disregarded or recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to declare B2B marketplace sales revenue; issuance of false or inflated invoices; deliberate omission of non-resident partner profit allocations; destruction of transaction records; using undisclosed AliPay or SWIFT settlement accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default assessment of the full taxable base, 0.6% monthly late-payment interest, administrative fines up to EUR 5,000, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud carrying fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Courts may order confiscation of assets equal to the evaded tax and damages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner, manager, or director engaged in the fraudulent scheme may be held jointly and severally liable for the SCSp's tax debts under veil-piercing principles. Criminal conviction can result in imprisonment, disqualification from management, seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and extradition or red-notice proceedings where flight risk exists.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated management fees, platform royalties, or procurement margins to a related entity in a no-tax or low-tax jurisdiction; absence of a written intragroup agreement; no functional analysis or benchmarking; no aggregate TP file; cash flows booked offshore without economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax authority will recharacterize the transactions at arm's length, disallow the non-arm's-length deductions, assess additional CIT, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax, and apply late-payment interest. Failure to produce TP documentation on request is independently penalized and may also trigger criminal tax penalties if the manipulation is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers who sign false TP certificates, prepare fictitious invoices, or knowingly execute artificial arrangements can be personally liable for restitution of the tax loss and may be prosecuted as accomplices to tax evasion. Directorial debarment and travel restrictions may accompany criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Tax Transparency Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no physical office in Luxembourg, no employees, no local bank account, no local governance, no business records, and no commercially rational decision-making; all platform operations are performed in another jurisdiction; Luxembourg address is used only to obtain treaty benefits or a favorable tax classification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Substance-over-form recharacterization; denial of tax transparency treatment; reallocation of profits to the place of effective management; denial of DTA benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; registration may be struck out by the Luxembourg trade register; tax debts are reassessed with interest and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee managers, general partners, and beneficial owners who operate the SCSp as a sham may have the corporate veil pierced for the full reassessed tax liability. Courts may issue director disqualification orders, asset freezes, travel bans, and criminal penalties for abuse of law where fraudulent intent is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering / Unauthorized Payment Processing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing B2B marketplace payments via AliPay and SWIFT without conducting customer due diligence or KYB/KYC checks; failing to register as a payment-service or e-money institution where funds are held or passed on; transacting with sanctioned persons or entities; converting platform turnover through opaque partner withdrawals to hide beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enforcement by the CSSF and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit. Administrative fines may reach up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; criminal money laundering penalties include fines up to EUR 5,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. The court may order asset freezing, confiscation, and disgorgement of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executive directors and the general partner face personal criminal liability for AML failures, private damages claims, attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and imprisonment. Regulators may also impose temporary or permanent bans from managing financial or commercial entities.
